definition_zh: 好的；擅长的；令人愉快的
definition_en: of high quality, skilled at something, or pleasant
core_image: 一只刚烤好的面包放在木桌上，香气扑鼻
scene: 这是一本好书。This is a good book.
sceneCN: 这里 good 是「好的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这是一本好书。

senses.title: Of high quality
senses.definition: of a high standard or quality
senses.definitionCN: 标准或品质很高的
senses.example: This is a good book.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一本好书。
senses.why: This is the broad sense of approval.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽泛的赞许含义。

senses.title: Skilled
senses.definition: able to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 能把某事做得很好的
senses.example: She is good at chess.
senses.exampleCN: 她擅长下棋。
senses.why: A person of good ability is good at a task.
senses.whyCN: 能力强的人，就是「擅长」某项任务。

senses.title: Pleasant
senses.definition: enjoyable and pleasing
senses.definitionCN: 令人享受和愉悦的
senses.example: We had a good time at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在聚会上玩得很开心。
senses.why: What is good for us is often pleasant to us.
senses.whyCN: 对我们有益的东西，往往也令我们愉快。

intro.en: Good is an old Germanic word that once meant fitting or suitable.
intro.cn: good 是一个古老的日耳曼词，最初意为合适、恰当。

items.en: God meant good, fit, or suitable.
items.cn: god 意为好的、合适的、恰当的。

items.en: The form became good and widened in meaning.
items.cn: 词形变为 good，含义变宽。

items.en: The comparative became better from another root.
items.cn: 比较级 better 来自另一个词根。

items.en: Good at extended it to skill.
items.cn: good at 把它扩展到「擅长」。

items.en: Good for extended it to benefit.
items.cn: good for 把它扩展到「有益」。

items.en: A good deal fixed it as a phrase of quantity.
items.cn: a good deal 把它固定为数量短语。

note.en: Good is compared with look-alike words and words of praise.
note.cn: 把 good 与形近词以及表示赞许的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Good is the general word for things that deserve a yes.
normalIntro.cn: good 是对值得说「是」的事物的一般说法。

normal.en: This is a good book.
normal.cn: 这是一本好书。

normal.en: She is good at chess.
normal.cn: 她擅长下棋。

normal.en: We had a good time at the party.
normal.cn: 我们在聚会上玩得很开心。

normal.en: Fresh air is good for you.
normal.cn: 新鲜空气对你有益。

normal.en: Good morning, everyone.
normal.cn: 大家早上好。

abstract.en: Good is a small word with a wide door.
abstract.cn: good 是一个词形小、门却很宽的字。

abstract.en: To be good at something is to give it attention.
abstract.cn: 擅长某事，就是把注意力给了它。

abstract.en: What is good for one may not be good for all.
abstract.cn: 对一人好的，未必对所有人都好。

examples.en: This is a good book.
examples.cn: 这是一本好书。

examples.en: She is good at chess.
examples.cn: 她擅长下棋。

examples.en: We had a good time at the party.
examples.cn: 我们在聚会上玩得很开心。

dict_mnemonic.text: good 的比较级是 better，最高级是 best；be good at 是「擅长」，be good for 是「对……有益」，a good deal 是「大量」；注意与 god（神）区分。

root: 来自古英语 god（好的、合适的），属日耳曼语族，比较级 better、最高级 best 来自另一词根，核心义为「符合标准的」。

sensesIntro.en: Good means of high quality, skilled at something, or pleasant.
sensesIntro.cn: good 意为品质优良、擅长某事，或令人愉快。

core.en: Something that meets the standard we hold.
core.cn: 符合我们所持标准的事物。

branches.en: A warm loaf waits on a wooden table.
branches.cn: 一只热面包放在木桌上。

branches.en: A player moves a piece with confidence.
branches.cn: 棋手自信地移动棋子。

branches.en: Friends laugh around a table.
branches.cn: 朋友们围桌欢笑。

branches.en: A good thing and a good hand both meet a standard.
branches.cn: 好东西与好手，都符合某种标准。

branches.en: Skill and enjoyment often grow together.
branches.cn: 技艺与享受，常常一起生长。

intro.en: Good has irregular comparison and a family of derived nouns.
intro.cn: good 有不规则比较级，并构成一族派生名词。

latinIntro.en: Good has no Latin root; it comes from Old English god.
latinIntro.cn: good 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 god。

definition_en: the quality of being kind and good, moral virtue, or an exclamation of surprise
core_image: 有人默默把伞递给雨中的陌生人，没有留下名字
scene: 她待人的善良人人皆知。Her goodness to others is well known.
sceneCN: 这里 goodness 是「善良」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她待人的善良人人皆知。

senses.title: Kindness
senses.definition: the quality of being kind to others
senses.definitionCN: 待人友善的品质
senses.example: Her goodness to others is well known.
senses.exampleCN: 她待人的善良人人皆知。
senses.why: This is the central moral sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最核心的道德含义。

senses.title: Moral virtue
senses.definition: excellence of character
senses.definitionCN: 品性上的优良
senses.example: The story praises the goodness of ordinary people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事赞美普通人的美德。
senses.why: Goodness names the quality behind good acts.
senses.whyCN: goodness 命名好行为背后的品质。

senses.title: An exclamation
senses.definition: a mild exclamation of surprise
senses.definitionCN: 表示惊讶的温和感叹
senses.example: Goodness, is it that late?
senses.exampleCN: 天哪，都这么晚了？
senses.why: People call on goodness as they call on heaven.
senses.whyCN: 人们呼唤「善良」，如同呼唤上天。

intro.en: Goodness is good plus the old noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: goodness 由 good 加古老的名词后缀 -ness 构成。

items.en: Godnes meant goodness or virtue.
items.cn: godnes 意为善良或美德。

items.en: The form became goodnesse and named a virtue.
items.cn: 词形变为 goodnesse，指一种美德。

items.en: It named the kindly quality of a person.
items.cn: 它指人善良的品质。

items.en: It also became a mild exclamation.
items.cn: 它也成为温和的感叹词。

items.en: Phrases like thank goodness fixed the exclamation.
items.cn: thank goodness 等短语固定了这一感叹用法。

note.en: Goodness is compared with look-alike words and words for virtue.
note.cn: 把 goodness 与形近词以及表示美德的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Goodness is good made into a substance you can see in a person.
normalIntro.cn: goodness 是把 good 变成在人身上看得见的品质。

normal.en: Her goodness to others is well known.
normal.cn: 她待人的善良人人皆知。

normal.en: The story praises the goodness of ordinary people.
normal.cn: 这个故事赞美普通人的美德。

normal.en: Goodness, is it that late?
normal.cn: 天哪，都这么晚了？

normal.en: Thank goodness you are safe.
normal.cn: 谢天谢地你平安无事。

normal.en: He believed in the goodness of human nature.
normal.cn: 他相信人性本善。

abstract.en: Goodness is kindness that does not need an audience.
abstract.cn: 善良，是不需要观众的善意。

abstract.en: The goodness of a person shows in small things.
abstract.cn: 一个人的善良，显在小事上。

abstract.en: Goodness given away is never lost.
abstract.cn: 给出去的善良，从不丢失。

examples.en: Her goodness to others is well known.
examples.cn: 她待人的善良人人皆知。

examples.en: The story praises the goodness of ordinary people.
examples.cn: 这个故事赞美普通人的美德。

examples.en: Goodness, is it that late?
examples.cn: 天哪，都这么晚了？

dict_mnemonic.text: goodness 由 good 加 -ness 构成；thank goodness 是「谢天谢地」，for goodness' sake 是「看在老天份上」，goodness knows 是「天知道」；注意与 goods（商品）区分。

root: 来自古英语 godnes（善良、美德），由 good 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，核心义为善良品性，后引申为感叹词。

sensesIntro.en: Goodness means kindness, moral virtue, or a mild exclamation of surprise.
sensesIntro.cn: goodness 指善良、美德，或温和的惊讶感叹。

core.en: A kind heart made visible in action.
core.cn: 在行动中显形的善心。

branches.en: A stranger holds an umbrella over another.
branches.cn: 陌生人为别人撑起伞。

branches.en: A story praises quiet decency.
branches.cn: 一个故事赞美安静的正直。

branches.en: A hand rises to the mouth in surprise.
branches.cn: 一只手惊讶地掩住嘴。

branches.en: Kind acts grow from a virtuous character.
branches.cn: 善行生长于美德的品格。

branches.en: People call on goodness when words fail.
branches.cn: 无言以对时，人们呼唤「善良」。

intro.en: Goodness joins good with the noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: goodness 由 good 加名词后缀 -ness 构成。

latinIntro.en: Goodness is Germanic; Latin uses bonitas for the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: goodness 属日耳曼语；拉丁语用 bonitas 表达同一概念。

items.example: She is a good person.
Her goodness to others is well known.
items.exampleCN: 她待人的善良人人皆知。

items.example: A goodly crowd gathered.
The children got goodies at the party.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们在聚会上得到了好东西。

items.exampleCN: 这份礼物是善意的表示。

Patience is a virtue.

definition_en: things made or bought for sale, or movable property in law
core_image: 仓库里堆满贴着标签的纸箱，叉车正把一箱箱货物运上货车
scene: 货车把货物运到仓库。The truck carried goods to the warehouse.
sceneCN: 这里 goods 是「商品、货物」（第 1 个义项）；句意：货车把货物运到仓库。

senses.title: Things for sale
senses.definition: things that are made or bought to be sold or used
senses.definitionCN: 为出售或使用而制造或购买的东西
senses.example: The truck carried goods to the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 货车把货物运到仓库。
senses.why: This is the everyday trading sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词日常的商业含义。

senses.title: Movable property
senses.definition: property that can be moved, as opposed to land, in law
senses.definitionCN: 法律上与土地相对、可以移动的财产
senses.example: The court divided the goods between the two heirs.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把动产分给了两位继承人。
senses.why: The old legal sense still survives in contracts and courts.
senses.whyCN: 这一古老的法律义在合同和法庭中仍然存在。

senses.title: Exactly what is wanted
senses.definition: the thing that is needed or promised, used informally
senses.definitionCN: 所需要或所承诺的东西，用于口语
senses.example: Her new album really delivers the goods.
senses.exampleCN: 她的新专辑确实不负所望。
senses.why: Informal speech uses the goods for what someone actually wants.
senses.whyCN: 口语用 the goods 表示人们真正想要的东西。

intro.en: Goods began as good things, then narrowed to things for trade.
intro.cn: goods 最初指「好东西」，后来收窄为用于交易的货物。

items.en: God meant good, and goods meant good things.
items.cn: god 意为好的，goods 意为好东西。

items.en: Goodes came to mean property and possessions.
items.cn: goodes 逐渐表示财产和所有物。

items.en: Goods narrowed to wares offered in trade.
items.cn: goods 收窄为市场上出售的商品。

items.en: Economists paired it with services.
items.cn: 经济学家把它与服务并列。

items.en: The old legal sense of movable property survived.
items.cn: 表示动产的古老法律义保留了下来。

note.en: Goods is compared with look-alike words and words for traded things.
note.cn: 把 goods 与形近词以及表示交易物的词作比较。

entries.definition: goods carried by ship or plane

normalIntro.en: Goods is the plural of good things turned into things for trade.
normalIntro.cn: goods 是「好东西」的复数，后来变成用来交易的货物。

normal.en: The truck carried goods to the warehouse.
normal.cn: 货车把货物运到仓库。

normal.en: The shop sells electrical goods.
normal.cn: 这家店出售电器商品。

normal.en: Goods and services are both part of trade.
normal.cn: 商品与服务都是贸易的一部分。

normal.en: The police found the stolen goods.
normal.cn: 警方找到了赃物。

normal.en: Her new album really delivers the goods.
normal.cn: 她的新专辑确实不负所望。

abstract.en: Goods move where money calls them.
abstract.cn: 货物往金钱呼唤的地方流动。

abstract.en: A thing becomes goods when hands begin to trade it.
abstract.cn: 当双手开始交易，东西就成了货物。

abstract.en: The worth of goods is a story told by the market.
abstract.cn: 货物的价值，是市场讲述的故事。

examples.en: The truck carried goods to the warehouse.
examples.cn: 货车把货物运到仓库。

examples.en: The court divided the goods between the two heirs.
examples.cn: 法院把动产分给了两位继承人。

examples.en: Her new album really delivers the goods.
examples.cn: 她的新专辑确实不负所望。

dict_mnemonic.text: goods 是 good（好的）的复数形式演变而来的名词，指「商品、货物」；consumer goods 是「消费品」，goods and services 是「商品与服务」，stolen goods 是「赃物」，deliver the goods 是「兑现承诺」。

root: 来自古英语 gōd（好的、财物），复数 goods 原指「好东西、财物」，后专指用于买卖的商品以及法律上的动产。

sensesIntro.en: Goods means things for sale, movable property in law, or informally exactly what is wanted.
sensesIntro.cn: goods 指出售的商品、法律上的动产，或口语中真正需要的东西。

core.en: Things that carry value and can be exchanged.
core.cn: 承载价值、可供交换的东西。

branches.en: Boxes leave a warehouse on a truck.
branches.cn: 纸箱被装上货车离开仓库。

branches.en: A court lists furniture and shares it out.
branches.cn: 法庭列出家具并加以分配。

branches.en: An album finally proves it was worth waiting for.
branches.cn: 一张专辑终于证明值得等待。

branches.en: Traded wares and movable property are both owned things.
branches.cn: 交易的商品与动产，都是被拥有的东西。

branches.en: A promise kept and a product sold are both delivered goods.
branches.cn: 兑现的承诺与售出的产品，都是交付的「货」。

intro.en: Goods connects to the good family of words.
intro.cn: goods 与 good 这个词族相连。

latinIntro.en: Goods is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: goods 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The bag was full of goodies.
items.exampleCN: 袋子里装满了好吃的东西。

items.example: The child asked for a goody.
He is a good-tempered man.

definition_en: very beautiful or colourful, or extremely pleasant
core_image: 夕阳把整片天空染成金红，云层像被点燃一样层层铺开
scene: 夕阳把天空染成绚丽的橙色。The sunset turned the sky a gorgeous orange.
sceneCN: 这里 gorgeous 是「绚丽的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：夕阳把天空染成绚丽的橙色。

senses.title: Splendid in colour
senses.definition: extremely beautiful, rich, or bright in appearance
senses.definitionCN: 外观极其美丽、浓艳或明亮
senses.example: The sunset turned the sky a gorgeous orange.
senses.exampleCN: 夕阳把天空染成绚丽的橙色。
senses.why: This is the original sense of rich, showy beauty.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示浓艳、华美外观的本义。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: very pleasant or enjoyable, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 非常令人愉快或享受，用于口语
senses.example: We had a gorgeous time at the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海边度过了极好的时光。
senses.why: Everyday speech stretched beauty into general praise.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把美丽扩展为泛泛的赞美。

senses.title: Beautiful to look at
senses.definition: very attractive in appearance, often of a person
senses.definitionCN: 外貌非常吸引人，常指人
senses.example: She looked gorgeous in that dress.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿那条裙子美极了。
senses.why: People borrowed the word for striking personal beauty.
senses.whyCN: 人们借用这个词来形容动人的个人美貌。

intro.en: Gorgeous came from Old French gorgias, meaning elegant and finely dressed.
intro.cn: gorgeous 来自古法语 gorgias，意为优雅、衣着讲究。

items.en: Gorgias described a fashionable, elegant man.
items.cn: gorgias 形容时髦优雅的人。

items.en: Gorgeous entered English meaning showy and splendid.
items.cn: gorgeous 以华丽、辉煌之义进入英语。

items.en: It was used of rich colours and fine clothes.
items.cn: 它用来形容浓艳的色彩和华美的衣服。

items.en: It spread to landscapes and beautiful people.
items.cn: 它扩展到景色和美丽的人。

items.en: Informal speech made it a general word of praise.
items.cn: 口语使它成为泛泛的赞美词。

note.en: Gorgeous is compared with look-alike words and words for beauty.
note.cn: 把 gorgeous 与形近词以及表示美丽的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Gorgeous is beauty with the volume turned up.
normalIntro.cn: gorgeous 是被调高了音量的美。

normal.en: The sunset turned the sky a gorgeous orange.
normal.cn: 夕阳把天空染成绚丽的橙色。

normal.en: We had a gorgeous time at the beach.
normal.cn: 我们在海边度过了极好的时光。

normal.en: She looked gorgeous in that dress.
normal.cn: 她穿那条裙子美极了。

normal.en: The hotel room had a gorgeous view.
normal.cn: 酒店房间有壮丽的景色。

normal.en: It was gorgeous weather for a walk.
normal.cn: 那是适合散步的极好天气。

abstract.en: Gorgeous is the eye refusing to look away.
abstract.cn: 绚丽，是眼睛舍不得移开。

abstract.en: Colour becomes gorgeous when it stops apologising.
abstract.cn: 色彩不再收敛时，就成了绚丽。

abstract.en: Beauty at its loudest still needs a witness.
abstract.cn: 最美的美，也需要一个见证者。

examples.en: The sunset turned the sky a gorgeous orange.
examples.cn: 夕阳把天空染成绚丽的橙色。

examples.en: We had a gorgeous time at the beach.
examples.cn: 我们在海边度过了极好的时光。

examples.en: She looked gorgeous in that dress.
examples.cn: 她穿那条裙子美极了。

dict_mnemonic.text: gorgeous 源自古法语 gorgias，本指衣着讲究，现在表示「绚丽的、华丽的」，口语中也表示「极好的」；gorgeously 是「华丽地」，gorgeous view 是「壮丽的景色」。

root: 源自古法语 gorgias（优雅、时髦），可能与本指颈部饰物的 gorge 有关，本义为打扮华美，后泛指色彩绚丽的、美丽动人的与极好的。

sensesIntro.en: Gorgeous means splendid in colour, extremely good in speech, or strikingly beautiful.
sensesIntro.cn: gorgeous 指色彩绚丽的、口语中极好的，或外貌美丽动人的。

core.en: Beauty that floods the senses.
core.cn: 涌满感官的美。

branches.en: The whole sky burns gold and red.
branches.cn: 整片天空燃成金红。

branches.en: A day at the beach feels perfect.
branches.cn: 海边的一天感觉完美。

branches.en: A woman enters and the room turns.
branches.cn: 一位女子走进来，满室侧目。

branches.en: A sunset and a face can both stop the eye.
branches.cn: 落日与面容都能让目光停驻。

branches.en: Praise of a day and praise of a person share one word.
branches.cn: 赞美一天与赞美一人，共用一个词。

intro.en: Gorgeous forms adverbs, nouns, and emphatic phrases.
intro.cn: gorgeous 构成副词、名词和强调短语。

latinIntro.en: Gorgeous is French in origin and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: gorgeous 源自法语，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The sunset turned the sky a gorgeous orange.
items.exampleCN: 夕阳把天空染成绚丽的橙色。

items.example: She was gorgeously dressed.
The gorgeousness of the hall amazed us.
items.exampleCN: 大厅的华美让我们惊叹。

items.example: The river cut a deep gorge.

definition_zh: 天哪；哎呀；唉呀（表示惊讶或强调的感叹词）
definition_en: an exclamation used to show surprise, wonder, or emphasis, as a mild substitute for God
core_image: 突然看见意外之事时脱口而出的轻轻一声惊叹
scene: 小男孩推开家门，发现桌上放着一个巨大的生日蛋糕，蜡烛已经点燃。Gosh, I really wasn't expecting a party today!
sceneCN: 这里 gosh 是「天哪、哎呀」（第 1 个义项：表示惊讶的感叹词）；句意是男孩惊喜地喊出「天哪，我真没想到今天会有派对」。图中可辨识物件：生日蛋糕、蜡烛、餐桌。

pos.zh: 感叹词：天哪；哎呀；表示惊讶、赞叹或加强语气

collocations.zh: 我的天哪（较缓和的惊叹）

derivatives.zh: 同类委婉惊叹词，义为「天哪；哎呀」，与 gosh 功能相同，出自另一委婉替换
由 golly 加后缀构成的旧式玩偶名称，义为「布娃娃」，与惊叹义仅形式相关

senses.title: An exclamation of surprise
senses.definition: a mild exclamation showing surprise or astonishment at something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 表示惊讶、震惊的委婉感叹词，用于遇到意料之外的事情时
senses.example: Gosh, I had no idea this old shop was still open.
senses.exampleCN: 天哪，我完全不知道这家老店还开着。
senses.why: People needed a way to cry out in surprise without using a sacred name, so a softened sound took over that job.
senses.whyCN: 人们需要一种不用神圣名字也能喊出惊讶的方式，于是用一个弱化了的音承担了这个功能。

senses.title: An exclamation of admiration
senses.definition: an exclamation expressing wonder, delight, or admiration for something impressive
senses.definitionCN: 表示赞叹、欣喜的感叹词，用于看到令人佩服或喜爱的事物时
senses.example: Gosh, what a beautiful view from the top of the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 哇，山顶上的景色真美。
senses.why: The same burst of breath that signals shock also signals delight; only the feeling behind it changes.
senses.whyCN: 同一声脱口而出的气息既能表达震惊也能表达欣喜，区别只在背后的情绪。

senses.title: A mild intensifier
senses.definition: an exclamation used mainly to add emphasis or make a statement sound more sincere
senses.definitionCN: 主要用于加强语气或让话语听起来更真诚的感叹词
senses.example: Gosh, it was kind of you to drive all this way to help.
senses.exampleCN: 说真的，你专程开车过来帮忙，真是太好了。
senses.why: Once the exclamation becomes habitual, it drifts into pure emphasis, coloring the sentence rather than reacting to it.
senses.whyCN: 当这声感叹变成习惯用语后，它就滑向纯粹的加强语气，不再对具体事物作出反应，而是给整句话上色。

senses.title: A polite substitute for God
senses.titleCN: 委婉替换：避免直呼神圣之名
senses.definition: a euphemistic replacement for the word God, used to avoid taking a sacred name in vain
senses.definitionCN: 作为 God 的委婉替换词，用于避免直呼神圣之名，语气更礼貌得体
senses.example: She caught herself and said gosh instead of the sacred name.
senses.exampleCN: 她及时收住，改口说了声 gosh，没有直呼那个神圣的名字。
senses.why: The word was created precisely for this purpose: to keep the exclamation but strip away the sacred name inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词正是为此目的而造：保留惊叹的功能，但去掉其中神圣的名字。

senses.title: An expression of dismay
senses.definition: an exclamation used when something goes wrong, showing mild frustration or dismay
senses.definitionCN: 用于事情出岔子时表示轻微沮丧或懊恼的感叹词
senses.example: Gosh, I've left my keys on the bus again.
senses.exampleCN: 唉呀，我又把钥匙落在公交车上了。
senses.why: Surprise and frustration share the same trigger: reality breaks your expectation, and the word escapes before you can think.
senses.whyCN: 惊讶与懊恼的触发点相同：现实打破了预期，这个词在你来得及思考之前就脱口而出。

senses.title: A softener in conversation
senses.definition: an exclamation used to soften a question or statement and make it sound friendlier
senses.definitionCN: 用于软化提问或陈述语气、使话语显得更亲切随和的感叹词
senses.example: Gosh, could you tell me how to get to the station?
senses.exampleCN: 请问，您能告诉我车站怎么走吗？
senses.why: The sound is short and gentle, so speakers place it at the front of a sentence to lower its edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个音短促而柔和，说话人把它放在句首，用来磨平句子生硬的棱角。

senses.title: Storybook and children's speech
senses.definition: an exclamation strongly associated with children's speech, old comics, and polite storybook dialogue
senses.definitionCN: 带有儿童口语、旧式漫画和礼貌童话对白色彩的感叹词
senses.example: In the old comics, the hero always cried gosh when the villain appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧漫画里，每当反派出现，主角总会喊一声 gosh。
senses.why: Because it is inoffensive, writers gave it to children and polite characters, and that image stuck.
senses.whyCN: 因为它毫无冒犯性，作者们把它分配给孩子和彬彬有礼的角色，这种形象便固定了下来。

senses.title: By gosh: stubborn emphasis
senses.definition: in the phrase by gosh, used to insist on one's point with folksy determination
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 by gosh，以朴素的固执语气坚持自己的说法
senses.example: He promised that by gosh he would finish rebuilding the fence before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他保证说，无论如何也要赶在冬天前把栅栏修好。
senses.why: Swearing formulas like by God became softened into by gosh, keeping the insisting frame without the sacred word.
senses.whyCN: by God 一类起誓句式被弱化为 by gosh，保留了坚持表态的框架，却去掉了神圣的词。

intro.en: Gosh is a deliberately softened exclamation: English speakers altered the name of God so that they could cry out without taking it in vain.
intro.cn: gosh 是刻意弱化出来的感叹词：英语使用者改动了 God 的读音，以便既能脱口惊呼又不至于妄称神名。

items.en: *ghut- or *ghau- is generally reconstructed as the root behind the verb 'to call' and the noun 'that which is invoked'; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ghut- 或 *ghau- 是「呼喊」动词及「被呼唤者」名词背后的词根；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The word god, meaning the deity, was already in use; it may have developed from the calling root, though earlier explanations linked it to a Gothic tribal name.
items.cn: 表示神祇的 god 一词已在古英语中使用；一般认为它源自「呼喊」词根，但也有早期解释把它与哥特部落名联系起来。

items.en: Swearing by God was widespread and was widely condemned as blasphemy, so speakers began distorting the sacred name into softened forms.
items.cn: 以 God 起誓十分普遍，又普遍被斥为亵渎，于是说话人开始把神圣之名扭曲成弱化形式。

items.en: The spelling gosh is first recorded in 1757; the exact date of its spoken origin is uncertain, and it likely circulated in speech earlier.
items.cn: 拼写形式 gosh 首见于 1757 年的记录；其口头起源的确切年代不确定，可能在此之前已在口语中流传。

items.en: Alongside gosh grew a whole family of softened exclamations such as golly and gollywog, all built by altering a name or sound rather than inventing a root.
items.cn: 十九世纪前后，gosh 周围长出一整族弱化惊叹词，如 golly 和 gollywog，它们都靠改动名字或读音构成，而非新造词根。

items.en: Today gosh survives mostly in children's speech, storybooks, and gently old-fashioned dialogue, while stronger exclamations have taken over elsewhere.
items.cn: 如今 gosh 主要保留在儿童口语、童话故事和略带旧式的礼貌对白中，其他场合已被更强的惊叹词取代。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers softened exclamations and sound-alike words; the near-meaning group gathers other mild cries of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组收同一类弱化惊叹词与发音相近的词；近义组收其他表示轻微惊讶的感叹词。

entries.definition: A British mild exclamation of surprise, formed by the same softening process as gosh.
entries.definitionCN: 英式温和惊叹词，义为「天哪」，与 gosh 出自同一种弱化改音手法。

entries.definition: An old-fashioned name for a type of doll; it borrows golly but has nothing to do with surprise.
entries.definitionCN: 旧式玩偶的名称，义为「布娃娃」；借用了 golly 一词，但与惊讶之义无关。

entries.definition: A long deep cut or wound; merely sounds close and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「深长的伤口；划开」；只是发音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A fierce hunting hawk; the first element is Old English for goose, unrelated to the exclamation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「苍鹰」；首成分是古英语「鹅」一词，与感叹词 gosh 无关。

entries.definition: Thin transparent fabric; its spelling and sound resemble gosh but its origin lies elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纱布、薄纱」；拼写与发音和 gosh 相近，但词源毫不相干。

entries.definition: A mild American exclamation of surprise, likewise softened from Jesus.
entries.definitionCN: 美式温和惊叹词，义为「哎呀」，同样由 Jesus 弱化而来。

entries.definition: A strong exclamation of astonishment or admiration, without any religious background.
entries.definitionCN: 表示惊叹或赞叹的强烈感叹词，义为「哇」，没有任何宗教背景。

entries.definition: A polite exclamation of surprise, itself a shortened softened form of oh my God.
entries.definitionCN: 表示惊讶的礼貌感叹语，义为「我的天」，本身是 oh my God 的缩短弱化形式。

entries.definition: A dated exclamation of surprise that points upward instead of naming God directly.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧式的惊讶感叹词，义为「天哪」，以「上天」指代而不直呼神名。

entries.definition: A mild exclamation built on the abstract quality of God, as in goodness me.
entries.definitionCN: 温和感叹词，以「上帝的善性」婉转代称，如 goodness me 表示「天哪」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real softening of the name of God and the phrases where the word actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「God 的弱化」这一真实来历，以及这个词实际出现的常见短语。

normal.en: gosh is God with the ending changed: the exclamation keeps the cry but drops the sacred name.
normal.cn: gosh 就是 God 改了词尾：惊叹保留下来，神圣之名被换掉了。

normal.en: oh my gosh is the polite twin of oh my God.
normal.cn: oh my gosh 是 oh my God 的礼貌版本。

normal.en: The same softening family gives gee (from Jesus) and golly, all mild cries of surprise.
normal.cn: 同一弱化家族还产出 gee（源自 Jesus）和 golly，都是温和的惊呼声。

normal.en: by gosh keeps the old swearing frame 'by God' in a folksy softened way.
normal.cn: by gosh 以朴素弱化的方式保留了 by God 这一古老的起誓句式。

normal.en: Old comics give gosh to children and polite heroes, so the word carries an innocent flavor.
normal.cn: 旧漫画把 gosh 留给孩子和礼貌的主角，因此这个词自带天真无害的色彩。

abstract.en: Picture a small child lifting both hands at a birthday cake, letting out one soft syllable of pure surprise.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小孩面对生日蛋糕举起双手，轻轻吐出一声纯粹的惊讶。

abstract.en: Hear the difference: one word shouts a sacred name, the other lets the air out gently, like a valve releasing pressure slowly.
abstract.cn: 听听两者的差别：一个词喊出神圣之名，另一个把气轻轻放掉，像阀门缓缓释放压力。

abstract.en: Gosh is a cushion between you and the shock: the event hits, and the soft sound absorbs it.
abstract.cn: gosh 是你与震惊之间的一块软垫：事件砸过来，柔和的一声把它吸收掉。

examples.en: Gosh, I had no idea this old shop was still open.
examples.cn: 天哪，我完全不知道这家老店还开着。

examples.en: Gosh, it was kind of you to drive all this way to help.
examples.cn: 说真的，你专程开车过来帮忙，真是太好了。

examples.en: The villagers still tell how the frightened child simply said gosh and then burst out laughing.
examples.cn: 村民至今还在讲，当年那个受惊的孩子只轻轻说了声「天哪」，接着便大笑起来。

root: gosh 是 God 的委婉弱化形式：把神圣之名的词尾改掉，保留惊叹功能而避免妄称神名。God 源自古英语 god「神」，一般追溯至原始印欧语表示「呼喊」的词根 *ghut- 或 *ghau-（重构形式，更早来源不确定）。与 golly、gee 等同属十九世纪前后的弱化惊叹词家族。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of gosh all grow from one softened cry: it signals surprise, delight, dismay, polite emphasis, and the innocent flavor of storybook speech.
sensesIntro.cn: gosh 的各个义项都从一声弱化的惊呼长出：它表示惊讶、赞叹、懊恼、礼貌的强调，以及童话语言的天真色彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft burst of breath escaping at an unexpected sight, like a valve gently releasing pressure.
core.cn: 核心意象：看到意外之事时轻轻呼出的一口气，像阀门缓缓释放压力。

branches.en: THE REACTION: unexpected events pull out the cry, whether the feeling is astonishment or mild dismay.
branches.cn: 反应线：意外之事逼出这声惊呼，情绪可以是震惊也可以是轻微懊恼。

branches.en: THE DELIGHT: the same breath turns admiring when the sight pleases instead of shocks.
branches.cn: 赞叹线：当所见令人欣喜而非震惊，同一声气息便转为赞叹。

branches.en: THE EMPHASIS: habitual use makes the word a soft intensifier and keeps the old swearing frame in by gosh.
branches.cn: 强调线：习惯化使这个词成为柔和的语气词，并在 by gosh 中保留古老的起誓框架。

branches.en: THE SUBSTITUTE: the word exists precisely to replace the sacred name while keeping the cry.
branches.cn: 替换线：这个词的存在意义正是替下神圣之名，同时保留惊叹。

branches.en: THE TONE: its softness softens questions and marks children's speech and storybook dialogue.
branches.cn: 语气线：它的柔和既可软化提问，也标示出儿童口语与童话对白的色彩。

intro.en: Gosh has no prefix or suffix: it is an altered form of the name of God, and its family is built by sound change rather than affixation.
intro.cn: gosh 没有前缀或后缀：它是 God 之名的改音形式，其词族靠读音变化而非词缀构词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word belongs to this family; the lineage runs through Old English god and a reconstructed Indo-European root, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词族没有拉丁同源词；其谱系经由古英语 god 与重构的印欧词根，因此拉丁同源词列表为空。

items.exampleCN: gosh 通过改动这个名字来弱化惊叹。

items.example: The root is generally reconstructed behind god.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为这个重构词根是 god 的来源。

items.meaning: changed ending used to soften a name

items.exampleCN: God 改变词尾就成了 gosh。

items.example: Golly grew beside gosh in the same softening family.

items.meaning: a mild cry softened from Jesus
items.meaningCN: 由 Jesus 弱化来的温和惊呼声

items.exampleCN: gee 显示同样的手法用在另一个神圣之名上。

items.meaning: polite version of oh my God

items.exampleCN: 我的天哪，这蛋糕太大了！

items.meaning: folksy insistence, softened from by God

definition_en: to rule a country or group, to control an organization, or to determine how something works
core_image: 船长站在船尾握着舵轮，目光越过海面看向远处的港口
scene: 这个国家由议会统治。The country is governed by a parliament.
sceneCN: 这里 govern 是「统治、治理」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个国家由议会统治。

senses.title: To rule
senses.definition: to control and direct the affairs of a country
senses.definitionCN: 控制并指导国家事务
senses.example: The country is governed by a parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家由议会统治。
senses.why: This is the central political sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词核心的政治含义。

senses.title: To manage
senses.definition: to direct the work of an organization or group
senses.definitionCN: 指导组织或团体的工作
senses.example: She governs the day-to-day work of the office.
senses.exampleCN: 她掌管办公室的日常工作。
senses.why: Running any body of people borrows the language of rule.
senses.whyCN: 管理任何一群人，都借用了统治的语言。

senses.title: To determine
senses.definition: to control or decide how something happens
senses.definitionCN: 控制或决定某事如何发生
senses.example: Strict rules govern how the money is spent.
senses.exampleCN: 严格的规定支配着这笔钱的使用。
senses.why: Rules steer actions just as a government steers a country.
senses.whyCN: 规则引导行动，正如政府引导国家。

intro.en: Govern began as a Latin word for steering a ship.
intro.cn: govern 最初是拉丁语中表示掌舵行船的词。

items.en: Gubernare meant to steer or pilot a ship.
items.cn: gubernare 意为掌舵、驾驶船只。

items.en: Governer kept the image of steering.
items.cn: governer 保留了掌舵的意象。

items.en: Govern entered English meaning to rule or direct.
items.cn: govern 以统治、指导之义进入英语。

items.en: It spread from states to offices and families.
items.cn: 它从国家扩展到办公室和家庭。

items.en: Rules and laws came to govern behaviour.
items.cn: 规则和法律开始支配行为。

note.en: Govern is compared with look-alike words and verbs of control.
note.cn: 把 govern 与形近词以及表示控制的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To govern is to hold the wheel of something larger than yourself.
normalIntro.cn: govern 就是握住比自身更大的事物的舵轮。

normal.en: The country is governed by a parliament.
normal.cn: 这个国家由议会统治。

normal.en: She governs the day-to-day work of the office.
normal.cn: 她掌管办公室的日常工作。

normal.en: Strict rules govern how the money is spent.
normal.cn: 严格的规定支配着这笔钱的使用。

normal.en: The island is self-governing.
normal.cn: 这座岛实行自治。

normal.en: Fear should not govern your choices.
normal.cn: 恐惧不应支配你的选择。

abstract.en: To govern well is to steer without gripping too hard.
abstract.cn: 善治，是掌舵而不死死抓紧。

abstract.en: Every system is governed by what it refuses to see.
abstract.cn: 每个体系都被它拒绝看见的东西所支配。

abstract.en: Power governs others; wisdom governs power.
abstract.cn: 权力统治他人，智慧统治权力。

root: 来自拉丁语 gubernare（掌舵、驾驶船只），经古法语 governer 进入英语，由掌舵的意象引申为治理国家、管理组织与支配事物。

branches.en: An office runs on one steady hand.

definition_en: an informal word for a grandmother, or an elderly woman in general

scene: 孩子们放学跑进院子，老远就喊了起来。Granny waved from under the apple tree.

senses.title: An affectionate word for grandmother
senses.definition: an informal, loving name for a grandmother
senses.definitionCN: 对祖母的非正式爱称
senses.example: Granny baked cookies with us on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶周日和我们一起烤饼干。
senses.why: The core image is a child's own name for the family elder.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是孩子自己给家中长者起的名字。

senses.title: Any elderly woman
senses.definition: an informal word for any old woman
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何年长女性的口语说法
senses.example: A kind granny showed us the way.
senses.exampleCN: 一位热心老大娘给我们指了路。
senses.why: The family name opens its door to strangers of the same age.
senses.whyCN: 家人的称呼向同龄的陌生老人敞开了门。

senses.title: Old-fashioned or fussy style
senses.definition: a style seen as old-fashioned, like granny clothes
senses.definitionCN: 被视为过时的、像老人衣着的风格
senses.example: That granny sweater is back in fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 那种老奶奶毛衣又流行回来了。
senses.why: The person's name becomes the style itself.
senses.whyCN: 人的称呼变成了风格的名字。

items.cn: 现代英语后来在时尚语境中长出风格义。

definition_en: money given for a purpose, or to give or allow something
core_image: 一张盖着印章的资助批文放在桌上
scene: 学校获得了一笔研究补助金。The school received a research grant.
sceneCN: 这里 grant 是「补助金、拨款」（第 1 个义项）；句意：学校获得了一笔研究补助金。

senses.title: Money for a purpose
senses.definition: money given by an organization for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 机构为特定用途提供的款项
senses.example: The school received a research grant.
senses.exampleCN: 学校获得了一笔研究补助金。
senses.why: The noun sense is money formally given.

senses.title: Give or allow
senses.definition: to give or allow something formally

senses.exampleCN: 法院准许她出行。
senses.why: The verb sense is formal giving or permitting.
senses.whyCN: 动词义指正式的给予或允许。

senses.title: Admit as true

senses.exampleCN: 我承认这个计划有风险。
senses.why: Admitting a point is a kind of giving way.
senses.whyCN: 承认一点，也是一种让步。
